name: Democratic Kampuchea (Khmer Rouge)
native: កម្ពុជាប្រជាធិបតេយ្យ (Kâmpŭchéa Prâchéathippadey)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Cambodia
predecessors.text: the whole of Cambodia: the Khmer Republic fell to the Khmer Rouge when Phnom Penh was captured on 17 April 1975

successors.name: People's Republic of Kampuchea
successors.text: Cambodia, taken by the Vietnamese army and the KUFNS: 'On 7 January 1979, the PAVN entered Phnom Penh along with members of the KUFNS'

ledger.x: 1975: the Khmer Rouge capture Phnom Penh (17 April) and empty the city.
1975: the Khmer Rouge hold the country from the fall of the capital (17 April).
May 1975: the Khmer Rouge raid Vietnamese islands.
1976: the constitution of Democratic Kampuchea is promulgated (5 January); the Khmer Rouge 'abolished the Royal Government of National Union of Kampuchea (GRUNK; established in 1970)'.
7 January 1979: the border war ends in the fall of the capital.
January 1979: the Khmer Rouge lose the country.

wars.name: Cambodian-Vietnamese War
wars.outcome: Vietnam and the KUFNS overthrew Democratic Kampuchea: Phnom Penh fell on 7 January 1979 and the People's Republic of Kampuchea was set up on 8 January; the Khmer Rouge withdrew to the Thai border.

wars.name: Khmer Rouge border attacks on Thailand
wars.outcome: No change of border: 'Khmer Rouge forces attacked villages in the border areas of Thailand near Aranyaprathet.'

certainty.note: The land frontiers are the French-era surveyed lines; the sea border and the islands are disputed ('The Vietnamese refused to recognize the Brévié Line'; Poulo Wai, Phú Quốc and Thổ Chu changed hands in 1975), and the Vietnamese frontier…
